Reproducing Daume et al. (2024) from dandiset 001187¶

Paper: Daume, Kaminski, Salimpour, Gomez Palacio Schjetnan, Anderson, Valiante, Mamelak and Rutishauser (2024), "Persistent activity during working memory maintenance predicts long-term memory formation in the human hippocampus", Neuron 112, 3957-3968, doi:10.1016/j.neuron.2024.09.013.

Dataset: DANDI:001187, version 0.240904.2347 (doi:10.48324/dandi.001187/0.240904.2347). This is the version the paper cites (Data and Code Availability; key resources table), and it is the only published version; the draft has the same 46 assets and size.

Claims: claims/001187/10.1016-j.neuron.2024.09.013.yaml, written from the accepted author manuscript in PubMed Central (PMC11624075) with its supplement (Figures S1 to S4, Table S1), and checked by a second reader. Method details the claims file lacks are taken from the paper or its code (github.com/rutishauserlab/SBCAT-NO-release-NWB, commit 6d07204) and cited where used, here and in sbcat.py.

Claim Tested or blocked
sessions-and-neurons, table-s1-counts tested
behaviour-overall-accuracy, fig1c to fig1g, ltm-rt-confidence tested
category-neuron-counts, fig2b, fig2c, fig2e, fig2f tested (fig2c, fig2e, fig2f blocked after testing: the readings disagree)
fig3a to fig3h (nine claims) tested
ms-neuron-counts, fig4b, fig4c, fig4d, fig4e, fig4f tested (fig4f blocked after testing: the readings disagree)

The new LTM pictures have no category in the dataset's metadata; for fig4d their categories are taken from their images in the files (see that section).

Every number below is computed from the streamed files. Seeds are fixed, one generator per claim section.

import time
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import sbcat

T0 = time.time()
pd.set_option("display.width", 200)
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 30)
pd.set_option("display.max_rows", 200)
print("dandiset", sbcat.DANDISET, "version", sbcat.VERSION)

dandiset 001187 version 0.240904.2347

Data check¶

Every NWB file of the pinned version is streamed; the trial tables, the raw event times, the electrode locations and the spike times are read (not the waveforms or the stimulus images).

rows = []
for si, s in enumerate(S):
    ltm, wm = s["ltm"], s["wm"]
    conf = ltm.confidence.values
    resp_old = conf >= 4
    rows.append(dict(
        session=s["identifier"], subject=s["subject_id"], ses=s["session_id"], age=s["age"],
        sex=s["sex"], institution=s["institution"], units=len(s["spikes"]),
        hipp=int(sum(sbcat.area_of(l) == "hippocampus" for l in s["units"].location)),
        amyg=int(sum(sbcat.area_of(l) == "amygdala" for l in s["units"].location)),
        wm_trials=len(wm), load1=int((wm.loads == 1).sum()), load3=int((wm.loads == 3).sum()),
        ltm_trials=len(ltm), ltm_old=int((ltm.new_old == 1).sum()),
        conf_values="".join(str(v) for v in np.unique(conf)),
        acc_mismatch=int(np.sum((resp_old == (ltm.new_old.values == 1)).astype(int)
                                != ltm.response_accuracy.values)),
        unsorted_units=len(s["unsorted_units"]),
        variant=s["notes"].split("Experiment variant: ")[1][0]))
SES = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(SES.to_string())
print("\nsessions", len(SES), "subjects", SES.subject.nunique(), "units", SES.units.sum(),
      "hippocampus", SES.hipp.sum(), "amygdala", SES.amyg.sum())
print("locations:", sorted({l for s in S for l in s["units"].location}))
print("institutions in the files:", SES.institution.unique().tolist())
print("sessions by identifier suffix (site):",
      pd.Series([s.split("_")[-1].lstrip("P0123456789") for s in SES.session]).value_counts().to_dict())
print("sessions with fewer than 400 LTM trials:",
      SES.loc[SES.ltm_trials < 400, ["session", "ltm_trials", "ltm_old"]].values.tolist())
print("sessions with fewer than 140 WM trials:",
      SES.loc[SES.wm_trials < 140, ["session", "wm_trials"]].values.tolist())
print("confidence values outside 1 to 6:",

print("trials whose accuracy disagrees with 'old' = confidence 4 to 6:", SES.acc_mismatch.sum())

Event clock. The trial tables and the spikes are checked against each other below, by the response of the units to picture onset (the category selection decodes the picture category from spikes aligned to the WM table's picture onsets; shifting the onsets removes it), see the cell after the category selection.

Units and the rate filter (claims U)¶

In [4]:
rows = []
for si, s in enumerate(S):
    for ui, loc in enumerate(s["units"].location):
        wmr, ltmr = sbcat.global_rates(s["spikes"][ui], s["raw_WM"], s["raw_LTM"])
        rows.append(dict(si=si, ui=ui, session=s["identifier"], patient=s["subject_id"],
                         location=loc, area=sbcat.area_of(loc), rate_wm=wmr, rate_ltm=ltmr))
UN = pd.DataFrame(rows)
UN["keep"] = (UN.rate_wm >= 0.1) & (UN.rate_ltm >= 0.1)
print("global WM rate (Hz): %.3f to %.2f; LTM rate: %.3f to %.2f" % (
    UN.rate_wm.min(), UN.rate_wm.max(), UN.rate_ltm.min(), UN.rate_ltm.max()))
print(UN.groupby("area").keep.agg(["size", "sum"]))
K = UN[UN.keep].reset_index(drop=True)
print("kept", len(K), "removed", int((~UN.keep).sum()))

Duplicate recordings. Two sessions could hold the same recording deposited twice. For every pair of sessions, the trial tables and the spike trains are compared.

In [5]:
dups = []
sig = [(s["identifier"], s["wm"].timestamps_Encoding1.values, s["wm"].PicIDs_Encoding1.values,
        [len(x) for x in s["spikes"]]) for s in S]
for i in range(len(S)):
    for j in range(i + 1, len(S)):
        same_pics = np.array_equal(sig[i][2], sig[j][2])
        same_times = len(sig[i][1]) == len(sig[j][1]) and np.allclose(sig[i][1] - sig[i][1][0],
                                                                      sig[j][1] - sig[j][1][0])
        common_counts = len(set(sig[i][3]) & set(sig[j][3]) - {0})
        if same_times or common_counts > 2:
            dups.append((sig[i][0], sig[j][0], same_pics, same_times, common_counts))
print("session pairs with identical WM timing or more than 2 units of identical spike counts:", dups)
same_order = pd.Series([tuple(s["wm"].PicIDs_Encoding1) for s in S]).duplicated(keep=False)
print("sessions sharing the same picture sequence (expected for one task variant):",
      int(same_order.sum()))

session pairs with identical WM timing or more than 2 units of identical spike counts: []
sessions sharing the same picture sequence (expected for one task variant): 45

Checks of the description against the data, from the outputs above. The confidence column is described as 1 to 6 with no coding; the accuracy column agrees in every trial with 1 to 3 meaning "new" and 4 to 6 "old" (shown). One trial has the value 7 (shown); it counts as "old" under that coding, which agrees with its accuracy. The LTM table's load is 0 for new pictures and num_times_shown 0 for new pictures (shown). Response times are in seconds (0.135 to 56 s in WM; up to 130 s in LTM, where the picture stays until a response). The maintenance period lasts 2.53 to 3.20 s (the Methods say 2.55 to 2.85 s) and starts at the end of the last picture. Picture 1 lasts 1.57 to 2.04 s where the Methods say 2 s. The files name Cedars-Sinai for every session, which the identifiers contradict (shown). No session pair shares its trial timing or spike counts, so no recording is deposited twice; the 45 sessions sharing one picture sequence are the same task version. The same units are taken to be recorded in both tasks of a session (one sorting per session, as the Methods say). The clock check after the category selection supports a shared clock of spikes and trial tables where sessions have enough units.

Claim sessions-and-neurons¶

After excluding two sessions, 46 sessions are analysed, in which 883 single units pass the 0.1 Hz rate filter, 351 in the hippocampus and 532 in the amygdala, of 950 isolated.

Result: reproduced. The dandiset holds 46 sessions and 950 units; the rate filter removes 67 (7.1%) and leaves 351 hippocampal and 532 amygdala units, as the paper states. The recorded counts of Table S1 sum to 973.

Claim table-s1-counts¶

Per session, the numbers of recorded units in the hippocampus and the amygdala are those of Table S1.

Sessions are matched by the label in the file identifier (P54CS with session 2 is P54cs_2).

In [7]:
SES["label"] = [sbcat.s1_label(x) for x in SES.session]
kept_counts = K.groupby(["session", "area"]).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
SES["hipp_kept"] = SES.session.map(kept_counts.get("hippocampus", {})).fillna(0).astype(int)
SES["amyg_kept"] = SES.session.map(kept_counts.get("amygdala", {})).fillna(0).astype(int)
SES["wm_acc"] = [100 * s["wm"].response_accuracy.mean() for s in S]
SES["ltm_acc"] = [100 * s["ltm"].response_accuracy.mean() for s in S]
TS1 = SES.merge(S1, on="label", how="outer", indicator=True)
print("matched:", (TS1._merge == "both").sum(), " only in dandiset:",
      TS1.label[TS1._merge == "left_only"].tolist(), " only in Table S1:",
      TS1.label[TS1._merge == "right_only"].tolist())
TS1 = TS1[TS1._merge == "both"].copy()
TS1["match_before"] = (TS1.hipp == TS1.h_rec) & (TS1.amyg == TS1.a_rec)
TS1["match_after"] = (TS1.hipp_kept == TS1.h_rec) & (TS1.amyg_kept == TS1.a_rec)
TS1["match_either"] = TS1.match_before | TS1.match_after
print("sessions matching before the filter:", int(TS1.match_before.sum()), "after:",
      int(TS1.match_after.sum()), "under either:", int(TS1.match_either.sum()), "of", len(TS1))
print(TS1.loc[~TS1.match_either, ["label", "session", "hipp", "hipp_kept", "h_rec", "amyg",
                                  "amyg_kept", "a_rec"]].to_string())
dwm, dltm = TS1.wm_acc_x - TS1.wm_acc_y, TS1.ltm_acc_x - TS1.ltm_acc_y
print("\naccuracy against Table S1 (a check of the session match): max |WM diff| %.2f, "
      "max |LTM diff| %.2f points" % (dwm.abs().max(), dltm.abs().max()))
print(TS1.loc[(dwm.abs() > 0.15) | (dltm.abs() > 0.15),
              ["label", "wm_acc_x", "wm_acc_y", "ltm_acc_x", "ltm_acc_y", "ltm_trials"]].round(2).to_string())

Result: partially reproduced. 42 of the 46 sessions match Table S1's recorded counts before the rate filter (21 after it). Four differ: P1809jh (1 hippocampal unit against 6), P61cs_2 (1 against 2), P68cs (7 amygdala units against 17) and P82cs (17 against 24); the 23 missing units are the difference between Table S1's 973 and the 950 of the text. The session match is confirmed by the accuracies, which differ from Table S1 by at most 0.18 points (WM) and 1.52 points (LTM, in sessions with incomplete LTM tables).

Behaviour¶

Per session measures (claims S, L). High confidence is a rating of 1 or 6 (sure), low confidence 2 to 5. Sessions "with confidence ratings" leave out the one session whose ratings are only 1 and 6 (printed below), the patient the paper says "did not use confidence ratings" (Results, paragraph 2); the paper's code drops it the same way, as its low-confidence accuracy is undefined (plot_behavior.m).

In [8]:
from scipy.stats import norm
rows = []
for s in S:
    wm, ltm = s["wm"], s["ltm"]
    conf = ltm.confidence.values
    old = ltm.new_old.values == 1
    said_old = conf >= 4
    acc = ltm.response_accuracy.values.astype(float)
    hi = (conf == 1) | (conf == 6)
    unsure = (conf == 2) | (conf == 5)
    guess = (conf == 3) | (conf == 4)
    lo = ~hi
    rt = ltm.response_time.values
    rt5 = np.where(rt > 5, np.nan, rt)
    wrt = wm.response_time.values
    wrt5 = np.where(wrt > 5, np.nan, wrt)
    hit, fa = said_old[old].mean(), said_old[~old].mean()
    nh, nf = old.sum(), (~old).sum()
    hit_c = min(max(hit, 1 / (2 * nh)), 1 - 1 / (2 * nh))
    fa_c = min(max(fa, 1 / (2 * nf)), 1 - 1 / (2 * nf))
    L = ltm.load.values
    nts = ltm.num_times_shown.values
    rows.append(dict(
        session=s["identifier"], wm_acc=wm.response_accuracy.mean(), ltm_acc=acc.mean(),
        hit=hit, fa=fa, dprime=norm.ppf(hit_c) - norm.ppf(fa_c), rate_corrected=(hit != hit_c) or (fa != fa_c),
        wm_acc_l1=wm.response_accuracy[wm.loads == 1].mean(), wm_acc_l3=wm.response_accuracy[wm.loads == 3].mean(),
        wm_rt_l1=np.nanmean(wrt5[wm.loads == 1]), wm_rt_l3=np.nanmean(wrt5[wm.loads == 3]),
        wm_rt_l1_all=np.mean(wrt[wm.loads == 1]), wm_rt_l3_all=np.mean(wrt[wm.loads == 3]),
        n_hi=hi.sum(), n_unsure=unsure.sum(), n_guess=guess.sum(),
        acc_hi=acc[hi].mean() if hi.any() else np.nan,
        acc_lo_pooled=acc[lo].mean() if lo.any() else np.nan,
        acc_lo_avg=np.nanmean([acc[unsure].mean() if unsure.any() else np.nan,
                               acc[guess].mean() if guess.any() else np.nan]) if lo.any() else np.nan,
        rt_hi_all=rt[hi].mean(), rt_lo_pooled_all=rt[lo].mean() if lo.any() else np.nan,
        rt_lo_avg_all=np.nanmean([rt[unsure].mean() if unsure.any() else np.nan,
                                  rt[guess].mean() if guess.any() else np.nan]) if lo.any() else np.nan,
        rt_hi_5=np.nanmean(rt5[hi]), rt_lo_pooled_5=np.nanmean(rt5[lo]) if lo.any() else np.nan,
        rt_lo_avg_5=np.nanmean([np.nanmean(rt5[unsure]) if unsure.any() else np.nan,
                                np.nanmean(rt5[guess]) if guess.any() else np.nan]) if lo.any() else np.nan,
        hit_l1=said_old[old & (L == 1)].mean(), hit_l3=said_old[old & (L == 3)].mean(),
        hit_twice=said_old[old & (nts == 2)].mean(), hit_once=said_old[old & (nts == 1)].mean()))
BEH = pd.DataFrame(rows)
noconf = BEH.session[BEH.n_hi == [len(s["ltm"]) for s in S]].tolist()
print("sessions whose ratings are all high confidence:", noconf)
BEHC = BEH[~BEH.session.isin(noconf)]
print("sessions with confidence ratings:", len(BEHC))
print("sessions without guessing ratings:", BEHC.session[BEHC.n_guess == 0].tolist())
print(BEH.describe().T[["count", "mean", "std", "min", "max"]].round(3).to_string())

Claim behaviour-overall-accuracy¶

Patients answered 93.3% of WM trials and 70.3% of LTM trials correctly (d' 1.19), both above the 50% chance level.

Claim fig1d-wm-rt-load¶

WM responses are faster in load 1 than in load 3 trials.

In [11]:
from scipy.stats import t as st_t
rng = np.random.default_rng(103)
for lab, a, b in [("RT > 5 s missing (main)", "wm_rt_l1", "wm_rt_l3"),
                  ("all RTs (variant)", "wm_rt_l1_all", "wm_rt_l3_all")]:
    t, p, df = sbcat.perm_ttest_paired(BEH[a], BEH[b], rng)
    print(f"{lab}: load 1 {BEH[a].mean():.3f} s, load 3 {BEH[b].mean():.3f} s; t({df}) = {t:.2f} "
          f"(paper -4.29), perm p = {p:.3g} (below 0.0001: {p < 1e-4})")
print("WM trials with RT > 5 s:", int(sum((s["wm"].response_time > 5).sum() for s in S)))
# The criterion's bar, p < 0.0001, lies at the resolution of a 10,000-permutation test, so the
# p that test estimates is computed here with 2,000,000 sign flips (two-sided, |t| at least the
# observed), and the 10,000-permutation p is shown over 100 seeds.
d = (BEH.wm_rt_l1 - BEH.wm_rt_l3).values
t_obs = sbcat.t_paired(d)
rng = np.random.default_rng(1031)
exceed = sum(int(np.sum(np.abs(sbcat.t_paired(rng.choice([-1.0, 1.0], size=(100000, d.size)) * d))
                        >= abs(t_obs))) for _ in range(20))
print(f"main reading, 2,000,000 permutations: {exceed} with |t| >= {abs(t_obs):.3f}, "
      f"p = {exceed / 2000000:.2e} (95% upper bound {(exceed + 1.96 * np.sqrt(exceed)) / 2000000:.2e}); "
      f"parametric t(45) p = {2 * st_t.sf(abs(t_obs), 45):.2e}")
p10k = np.array([sbcat.perm_ttest_paired(BEH.wm_rt_l1, BEH.wm_rt_l3, np.random.default_rng(s))[1]
                 for s in range(100)])
print(f"10,000 permutations over 100 seeds: p below 0.0001 in {int(np.sum(p10k < 1e-4))}, "
      f"median p {np.median(p10k):.3g}, largest {p10k.max():.3g}")

RT > 5 s missing (main): load 1 1.393 s, load 3 1.525 s; t(45) = -4.28 (paper -4.29), perm p = 0.0003 (below 0.0001: False)
all RTs (variant): load 1 1.706 s, load 3 1.689 s; t(45) = 0.20 (paper -4.29), perm p = 0.859 (below 0.0001: False)
WM trials with RT > 5 s: 197

main reading, 2,000,000 permutations: 119 with |t| >= 4.279, p = 5.95e-05 (95% upper bound 7.02e-05); parametric t(45) p = 9.67e-05

10,000 permutations over 100 seeds: p below 0.0001 in 63, median p 0.0001, largest 0.0007

Result: reproduced. With response times above 5 s set to missing, load 1 is faster (1.393 against 1.525 s), t(45) = -4.28 as in the paper (-4.29). The criterion's bar, p < 0.0001, lies at the resolution of a 10,000-permutation test: the draw printed first gives p = 0.0003, and over 100 seeds 63 draws give p below 0.0001. With 2,000,000 permutations the p the test estimates is 6.0e-05 (95% upper bound 7.0e-05), below 0.0001, so the claim is graded reproduced. With all response times (variant), there is no difference (t = 0.20).

Category and memory-selective neurons (selections C and M)¶

Each kept unit is tested as the paper's code does (NWB_calcCatSelective_SB.m, NWB_calcMemSelective_SB.m), with 10,000 permutations. Seeds are standard choices.

In [16]:

Clock check. If the trial tables share the spikes' clock, the category of the picture on the screen is decodable from spikes aligned to the table's onsets and not from spikes aligned to onsets shifted away from the picture. The same holds for old against new in the LTM task. Per session, the fraction of units with a parametric one-way ANOVA (WM categories) or t-test (LTM old against new, correct trials) at p < 0.05, for the onsets as given and shifted by -5 s (into the preceding trial; a contrast between labels, not an offset).

In [17]:
from scipy import stats as st
rows = []
for si, s in enumerate(S):
    times, cats = sbcat.category_rates(s)
    ltm = s["ltm"]
    ok = ltm.response_accuracy.values == 1
    tl, old = ltm.timestamps_PicOnset.values[ok], ltm.new_old.values[ok] == 1
    for shift in (0.0, -5.0):
        nw = nl = 0
        for _, u in K[K.si == si].iterrows():
            sp = s["spikes"][u.ui]
            r = sbcat.count(sp, times + shift, 0.2, 1.2)
            if r.std() > 0 and st.f_oneway(*[r[cats == c] for c in np.unique(cats)]).pvalue < 0.05:
                nw += 1
            c = sbcat.count(sp, tl + shift, 0.2, 1.2)
            if c.std() > 0 and st.ttest_ind(c[old], c[~old]).pvalue < 0.05:
                nl += 1
        rows.append(dict(session=s["identifier"], shift=shift, units=int((K.si == si).sum()),
                         wm_sig=nw, ltm_sig=nl))
CLK = pd.DataFrame(rows).pivot(index="session", columns="shift", values=["units", "wm_sig", "ltm_sig"])
print(CLK.to_string())
tot = pd.DataFrame(rows).groupby("shift")[["units", "wm_sig", "ltm_sig"]].sum()
print(tot)
print("sessions where the true WM onsets give no more significant units than the shifted ones:",
      CLK.index[CLK[("wm_sig", 0.0)] <= CLK[("wm_sig", -5.0)]].tolist())
print("sessions where the true LTM onsets give no more significant units than the shifted ones:",
      CLK.index[CLK[("ltm_sig", 0.0)] <= CLK[("ltm_sig", -5.0)]].tolist())

Peri-onset rates (asked for in verification round 1). For every session, the mean rate of all its units around every WM picture onset (encoding pictures and probe) and every LTM picture onset, in 100 ms bins from -0.5 to 1.5 s, at the true onsets and at onsets shifted by -5 s. A shared clock shows as a change after the true onsets that the shifted onsets lack. Per session, the units whose count 0.1 to 0.6 s after onset differs from the count in the 0.5 s before (paired t-test over onsets, p < 0.01) are counted at both. The PSTHs are printed for the sessions listed above as having no advantage in the WM test.

In [18]:
EDGES = np.round(np.arange(-0.5, 1.5001, 0.1), 2)


def psth(spikes_list, onsets):
    """Mean rate (Hz) of the units in 100 ms bins around the onsets."""
    h = np.zeros(len(EDGES) - 1)
    for sp in spikes_list:
        h += np.diff(np.searchsorted(sp, onsets[:, None] + EDGES[None, :]), axis=1).sum(0)
    return h / (len(spikes_list) * len(onsets) * 0.1)


NOADV = CLK.index[CLK[("wm_sig", 0.0)] <= CLK[("wm_sig", -5.0)]].tolist()
rows, curves = [], []
for si, s in enumerate(S):
    sp = [s["spikes"][u.ui] for _, u in K[K.si == si].iterrows()]
    times, _ = sbcat.category_rates(s)
    r = dict(session=s["identifier"], no_wm_advantage=s["identifier"] in NOADV, units=len(sp))
    for task, on in (("WM", np.sort(times)), ("LTM", np.sort(s["ltm"].timestamps_PicOnset.values))):
        for shift, lab in ((0.0, "true"), (-5.0, "-5 s")):
            h = psth(sp, on + shift)
            r[f"{task} {lab}"] = sum(
                st.ttest_rel(sbcat.count(x, on + shift, 0.1, 0.6), sbcat.count(x, on + shift, -0.5, 0.0)).pvalue < 0.01
                for x in sp if len(x))
            if r["no_wm_advantage"]:
                curves.append(pd.Series(h, index=[f"{e:.1f}" for e in EDGES[:-1]],
                                        name=(s["identifier"], task, lab)))
    rows.append(r)
CLK2 = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print("units whose count 0.1 to 0.6 s after onset differs from the count in the 0.5 s before "
      "(paired t-test over onsets, p < 0.01), per session:")
print(CLK2.round(3).to_string(index=False))
for task in ("WM", "LTM"):
    more = CLK2[f"{task} true"] > CLK2[f"{task} -5 s"]
    print(f"{task}: units responding at the true onsets {int(CLK2[f'{task} true'].sum())}, at the shifted "
          f"{int(CLK2[f'{task} -5 s'].sum())}; sessions with more at the true onsets {int(more.sum())} of "
          f"{len(CLK2)}, of the {len(NOADV)} without a WM advantage {int(more[CLK2.no_wm_advantage].sum())}")
print("\nPSTHs (Hz, bin start in s) for the sessions without a WM advantage:")
print(pd.DataFrame(curves).round(2).to_string())

Across sessions, 193 units respond to WM picture onsets at the true times against 22 at the shifted ones, and 253 against 14 at LTM onsets. Of the 12 sessions without a WM advantage in the category test, nine have more responding units at the true onsets in the WM or the LTM task, four of them by a single unit. The other three cannot show it: sub-38 (P1903JHU) has no unit after the rate filter, sub-35 (P1809JHU) one, and sub-24 session 2 (P090TWH) has one responding unit at both the true and the shifted WM onsets and none in the LTM task. Their clock is assumed to be shared, as for the others; these three sessions hold 10 of the 883 units.

Claim category-neuron-counts¶

104 hippocampal units (29.65%) and 220 amygdala units (41.35%) are category neurons.

Tables of category neurons¶

For each category neuron, one row per encoding picture of every WM trial with its spike counts in the maintenance (0 to 2.5 s after maintenance onset), baseline (-0.9 to -0.3 s before picture 1) and picture 1 (0 to 2 s) windows, and, for pictures shown in the LTM test, that trial's accuracy and confidence (sbcat.picture_table, sbcat.add_counts).

Outliers for the GLMs of Figures 2 and 3 (claims O, as amended after a reader's answer in questions/001187.yaml): O-G, each neuron's mean normalized rate over all rows of its table before trial selection, as NWB_computeGLM.m computes it, the neuron removed when its mean lies outside the mean +- 3 SD of the neuron means (Methods, Statistics, "differed ±3 SD from the mean"); O-C, the code's rule (above 3 SD of the neuron means, no centring), as a variant; and no removal. Neurons with a zero baseline are dropped under all three.

In [20]:
PT = {si: sbcat.picture_table(S[si]) for si in sorted(K.si.unique())}
CN = K[K.cat].copy()
CN["neuron"] = [f"{a}_{b}" for a, b in zip(CN.si, CN.ui)]
NPT = {}
for _, u in CN.iterrows():
    pt = sbcat.add_counts(PT[u.si], S[u.si]["spikes"][u.ui])
    pt["pref"] = (pt.cat == u.pref).astype(int)
    pt["neuron"], pt["patient"], pt["area"] = u.neuron, u.patient, u.area
    NPT[u.neuron] = pt
print("category neurons:", len(NPT), " picture rows per neuron:",
      sorted({len(p) for p in NPT.values()}))
print("pictures shown in the LTM test per session: %d to %d" % (
    min(p.in_ltm.sum() for p in PT.values()), max(p.in_ltm.sum() for p in PT.values())))


def trial_rows(pt):
    """One row per WM trial; pref is true when any encoding picture is of the preferred
    category."""
    return pt.groupby("trial").agg(r_maint=("r_maint", "first"), r_bsl=("r_bsl", "first"),
                                   c_maint=("c_maint", "first"), c_bsl=("c_bsl", "first"),
                                   r_enc1=("r_enc1", "first"), acc=("acc_WM", "first"),
                                   load=("load", "first"), pref=("pref", "max"),
                                   neuron=("neuron", "first"), patient=("patient", "first"),
                                   area=("area", "first")).reset_index()


def code_rows(pt):
    """The rows of the paper's code (NWB_computeGLM.m): one per encoding picture later shown
    in the LTM test, pref per picture."""
    return pt[pt.in_ltm].rename(columns={"acc_WM": "acc"}).reset_index(drop=True)


def wm_table(neurons, rows, base, value="r_maint"):
    """Normalized rates (claims B) for the given neurons. rows 'trial' or 'code'; base 'B1'
    (mean baseline over all WM trials of the neuron) or 'B2' (over the rows of the code's
    table). Neurons with a zero baseline are dropped (their values are infinite)."""
    out = []
    for n in neurons:
        pt = NPT[n]
        tr = trial_rows(pt)
        d = tr if rows == "trial" else code_rows(pt)
        b = tr.r_bsl.mean() if base == "B1" else code_rows(pt).r_bsl.mean()
        if b == 0:
            continue
        d = d.copy()
        d["FR"] = sbcat.normalize(d[value], b)
        out.append(d)
    return pd.concat(out, ignore_index=True)


def fit_readings(neurons, select, formula, readings, value="r_maint"):
    """Fit the GLM under each reading; readings are (rows, base) pairs. Outliers by O-G
    (main, claims O) and O-C (variant), both on the neuron means over all rows of the table
    before selection, as NWB_computeGLM.m takes them, and none."""
    res = []
    for rows, base in readings:
        full = wm_table(neurons, rows, base, value)
        d = select(full)
        for orule in ("O-G", "O-C", "none"):
            bad = (sbcat.og_remove(full) if orule == "O-G" else
                   sbcat.oc_remove(full) if orule == "O-C" else set())
            dd = d[~d.neuron.isin(bad)]
            m = sbcat.mixedlm(dd, formula)
            for term, r in m.iterrows():
                res.append(dict(rows=rows, base=base, outliers=orule, term=term, beta=r.beta,
                                SE=r.SE, p=r.p, neurons=m.attrs["neurons"], n=m.attrs["n"],
                                removed=len(bad), converged=m.attrs["converged"]))
    return pd.DataFrame(res)


def show(res, terms=None):
    r = res if terms is None else res[res.term.isin(terms)]
    print(r.round({"beta": 2, "SE": 2, "p": 6}).to_string(index=False))


HIPP_CN = CN.neuron[CN.area == "hippocampus"].tolist()
AMYG_CN = CN.neuron[CN.area == "amygdala"].tolist()
READ4 = [("trial", "B1"), ("trial", "B2"), ("code", "B1"), ("code", "B2")]

Claim fig2c-hippocampus-correct-load¶

When the preferred category is held, hippocampal category neurons fire more in correct than incorrect trials and more in load 1 than load 3 trials.

Trials holding a preferred picture, correct and incorrect, both loads (one row per trial); acc (incorrect the reference) and l1 (load 1 against load 3). Readings: (a) main effects, (b) with their interaction; baseline B1 or B2.

def pref_trials(d):
    d = d[d.pref == 1].copy()
    d["l1"] = (d.load == 1).astype(int)
    # -0.5/+0.5 coding: with the interaction, acc_c and l1_c are main effects (averaged over
    # the other factor), where acc and l1 in "acc * l1" are effects at the reference level
    d["acc_c"], d["l1_c"] = d.acc - 0.5, d.l1 - 0.5
    return d

Result: blocked (methods underspecified). The readings the criterion names give different outcomes, and the claims file blocks such a claim. With main effects only (reading a) and O-G, baseline B1 gives accuracy 18.48 (p = 0.0499) and load 18.64 (p = 0.0003), both positive at p < 0.05 with both betas above tolerance (16.22 +- 1.62 and 13.769 +- 1.377); B2 gives load 12.94 (p = 0.0069, within tolerance) and accuracy 16.46 (p = 0.060). Both grade the claim partially reproduced. With the interaction term (reading b), the load term is negative and not significant (-14.24, p = 0.56 with B1; -18.66, p = 0.41 with B2), which grades it not reproduced. In "acc * l1" with 0/1 coding, that term is the load effect in incorrect trials (59 rows with load 1), not a main effect; with -0.5/+0.5 coding (a variant, not a reading of the claims file) the load main effect is 2.96 (p = 0.81) with B1 and -2.12 (p = 0.86) with B2, and accuracy 30.62 (p = 0.018) and 28.09 (p = 0.019). Whether reading (b) is the paper's model is asked of a reader (questions/001187.yaml). O-C gives accuracy 18.68 (p = 0.028) and load 13.63 (p = 0.0034) under reading (a) with B1.

Result: blocked (methods underspecified). The readings the criterion names give different outcomes, and the claims file blocks such a claim. The accuracy effect has p >= 0.05 under every reading and outlier rule (with O-G p from 0.19 to 0.24, betas -6.39 to -7.44; paper -6.13, p = 0.24). With main effects (reading a), B1 and O-G the load effect is 11.55 (p = 0.00002), within 12.309 +- 1.231, which grades the claim reproduced. With B2 it is 9.51 (p = 0.00025), below tolerance, and with the interaction term (reading b) it is not significant (p = 0.70 with B1, 0.82 with B2); these grade it partially reproduced. As for fig2c, the load term of reading (b) is the effect in incorrect trials; with -0.5/+0.5 coding (a variant) the load main effect is 8.67 (p = 0.24) with B1 and 6.47 (p = 0.36) with B2. O-C gives the same as O-G with B1.

The table of Figure 3 (NWB_computeGLM.m)¶

One row per WM picture later shown in the LTM test; rate 0 to 2.5 s after maintenance onset, normalized to the mean baseline over all the neuron's rows (B, as the code); then rows kept when the WM trial was correct and the picture is of the preferred category. Confidence is recoded as the Methods say (sbcat.conf3_code). The session whose ratings are all sure is left out of these confidence analyses (Results, paragraph 2); the code keeps it, shown as a variant. Area: hipp = 1 for hippocampus, amygdala the reference.

In [25]:
NOCONF_SI = [si for si, s in enumerate(S) if s["identifier"] in noconf]


def fig3_full(neurons, value="r_maint"):
    d = wm_table(neurons, "code", "B2", value)
    d["hipp"] = (d.area == "hippocampus").astype(int)
    d["conf3"] = sbcat.conf3_code(d.conf)
    d["si"] = [int(n.split("_")[0]) for n in d.neuron]
    return d


def fig3_select(d, pref=1, keep_noconf=False):
    d = d[(d.acc == 1) & (d.pref == pref) & d.conf.notna()]
    if not keep_noconf:
        d = d[~d.si.isin(NOCONF_SI)]
    return d


ALL_CN = HIPP_CN + AMYG_CN
F3FULL = fig3_full(ALL_CN)
F3 = fig3_select(F3FULL)
print("rows", len(F3), "neurons", F3.neuron.nunique(), "by area:",
      F3.groupby("area").neuron.nunique().to_dict())
print("rows by LTM accuracy and confidence:", F3.groupby(["LTMacc", "conf3"]).size().to_dict())
print("neurons dropped for a zero baseline:", len(ALL_CN) - F3FULL.neuron.nunique())
print("FR (%% change) range: %.1f to %.1f" % (F3.FR.min(), F3.FR.max()))


def fig3_fit(data_full, formula, select=fig3_select, outlier_pool=None, label=""):
    """Fit under O-G (main, claims O), O-C (variant) and none. Both rules take each neuron's
    mean over all its rows of the full table, before trial selection, as NWB_computeGLM.m
    does; outlier_pool is that full table when it is not data_full (outliers found over both
    areas for a model of one area)."""
    d = select(data_full)
    pool = data_full if outlier_pool is None else outlier_pool
    res = []
    for orule in ("O-G", "O-C", "none"):
        bad = (sbcat.og_remove(pool) if orule == "O-G" else
               sbcat.oc_remove(pool) if orule == "O-C" else set())
        dd = d[~d.neuron.isin(bad)]
        m = sbcat.mixedlm(dd, formula)
        for term, r in m.iterrows():
            res.append(dict(reading=label, outliers=orule, term=term, beta=r.beta, SE=r.SE, p=r.p,
                            neurons=m.attrs["neurons"], n=m.attrs["n"], removed=len(bad),
                            converged=m.attrs["converged"]))
    return pd.DataFrame(res)

In a GLM over category neurons of both areas, no main effect of LTM accuracy, confidence or area is significant, nor the LTM accuracy by confidence interaction, but every interaction with area is, so the relation of maintenance activity to later memory differs between hippocampus and amygdala.

Result: partially reproduced. With O-G (5 neurons removed, 313 remain) the three interactions with area are significant with the paper's signs (LTM accuracy x area 70.57, p = 0.0011; confidence x area 19.12, p = 0.019; three-way -32.52, p = 0.0017) and no main effect or the accuracy x confidence term is (smallest p 0.24), but all three betas are larger than the paper's and outside tolerance (59.78 +- 5.98, 16.88 +- 1.69, -28.64 +- 2.86). With the all-sure session kept, as the code does, 73.60, 20.23 and -33.74. The code's rule (O-C, variant, 8 removed) gives 56.61, 16.60 and -27.83, all within tolerance, and with the all-sure session kept 59.96, 17.84 and -29.16.

Claim fig3b-hippocampus-predicts-ltm¶

In the hippocampus, maintenance activity of category neurons for the preferred category predicts later LTM accuracy and confidence, with an interaction between the two, so activity is higher for pictures later remembered than forgotten.

Claims fig3c-hippocampus-high-confidence and fig3d-amygdala-no-difference¶

Across hippocampal category neurons, maintenance firing for the preferred category is higher for pictures later remembered than forgotten with high confidence, but not with low confidence.

Across amygdala category neurons, maintenance firing does not differ between later remembered and forgotten pictures, with high or low confidence.

Rows of the Figure 3 table (correct WM trials, preferred pictures later tested, the all-sure session left out). High: remembered rating 6 against forgotten rating 1; low: remembered 4 or 5 against forgotten 2 or 3. Per neuron the mean rate per condition; neurons without rows or without spikes in a condition, with a zero baseline, or outside mean +- 3 SD of the neuron and condition values of the test (O-M) are removed; paired permutation t-test (P). Readings: (a) normalized rate, (b) spikes per second.

CONDS = {"high": ([6], [1]), "low": ([4, 5], [2, 3])}


def remembered_forgotten(area, level, value, rng, data=None):
    d = F3 if data is None else data
    d = d[d.area == area]
    rem, forg = CONDS[level]
    col = "FR" if value == "norm" else "r_maint"
    a = d[d.conf.isin(rem)].groupby("neuron").agg(v=(col, "mean"), c=("c_maint", "sum"))
    b = d[d.conf.isin(forg)].groupby("neuron").agg(v=(col, "mean"), c=("c_maint", "sum"))
    j = a.join(b, lsuffix="_r", rsuffix="_f", how="inner")
    n_both = len(j)
    j = j[(j.c_r > 0) & (j.c_f > 0)]
    n_spk = len(j)
    vals = j[["v_r", "v_f"]].values
    out = np.any(np.abs(vals - vals.mean()) > 3 * vals.std(ddof=1), axis=1)
    j = j[~out]
    t, p, df = sbcat.perm_ttest_paired(j.v_r, j.v_f, rng)
    return dict(area=area, level=level, value=value, with_both=n_both, with_spikes=n_spk,
                n=len(j), mean_rem=j.v_r.mean(), mean_forg=j.v_f.mean(),
                diff=(j.v_r - j.v_f).mean(), t=t, df=df, p=p), j.index.tolist()


rng = np.random.default_rng(301)
R3CD, KEEP3C = [], {}
for area in ("hippocampus", "amygdala"):

        for value in ("norm", "Hz"):
            r, kept = remembered_forgotten(area, level, value, rng)
            R3CD.append(r)
            KEEP3C[(area, level, value)] = kept

Result: not reproduced. In the hippocampus, remembered and forgotten do not differ with high confidence under either reading (normalized: t(68) = 1.17, p = 0.26; spikes per second: t(70) = 1.79, p = 0.078), nor with low confidence (p = 0.30 and 0.10). Keeping the all-sure session, as the code does, gives p = 0.33 and 0.054. 69 to 71 neurons enter the high-confidence test against 83 in the paper. The table of losses shows where they go: of 102 category neurons, 100 are outside the all-sure session and have rows, 98 have a remembered high-confidence row, 82 a forgotten one, 80 both, 73 spikes in both, and O-M removes 4 or 2 more. The forgotten condition has a median of 5 rows per neuron, and 13 neurons have one. Since 80 neurons have both conditions before any removal, fewer than the 83 the paper tests, the paper's rows likely differ from the claims file's (correct WM trials, preferred pictures later tested). Taking incorrect WM trials too (a diagnostic) leaves 80 neurons with both conditions and gives p = 0.46 and 0.12.

Claims fig3e-early-delay-cluster and fig3f-amygdala-no-cluster¶

In hippocampal category neurons, firing differs between pictures later remembered and forgotten with high confidence early in the maintenance period, from 0 to 650 ms.

In amygdala category neurons, no period of the maintenance period shows a significant difference between later remembered and forgotten pictures.

Neurons and conditions of the high-confidence test of fig3c (and fig3d), per reading of the rate. Time-resolved rates over 0 to 2.5 s after maintenance onset: (a) 200 ms windows stepped by 25 ms, centres 0 to 2.5 s (windows reach 100 ms past the period at both ends), or (b) 50 ms bins, centres 25 ms to 2.475 s. Normalized rates use each neuron's mean baseline rate of the Figure 3 table. Cluster-based permutation test (sbcat.cluster_test), 10,000 sign flips, cluster-forming threshold two-sided 0.05, cluster p judged at 0.025.

In [33]:
BINNINGS = {"(a) 200/25 ms": (np.arange(0, 2.5001, 0.025), 0.2),
            "(b) 50 ms": (np.arange(0.025, 2.5, 0.05), 0.05)}
BASE3 = {n: g.r_bsl.mean() for n, g in F3FULL.groupby("neuron")}
NEURON_SPIKES = {n: S[u.si]["spikes"][u.ui] for n, u in CN.set_index("neuron").iterrows()}


def time_resolved(area, value, binning, rng):
    centres, width = BINNINGS[binning]
    neurons = KEEP3C[(area, "high", value)]
    d = F3[(F3.area == area) & F3.neuron.isin(neurons)]
    A, B = [], []
    for n in neurons:
        g = d[d.neuron == n]
        rates = []
        for confs in ([6], [1]):
            t0 = g.t_maint[g.conf.isin(confs)].values
            r = sbcat.binned_counts(NEURON_SPIKES[n], t0, centres, width).mean(0) / width
            rates.append(sbcat.normalize(r, BASE3[n]) if value == "norm" else r)
        A.append(rates[0])
        B.append(rates[1])
    t, cl = sbcat.cluster_test(np.array(A), np.array(B), rng)
    return centres, t, cl, len(neurons)


R3EF, TCURVE = [], {}
t0 = time.time()
for area in ("hippocampus", "amygdala"):
    for value in ("norm", "Hz"):
        for binning in BINNINGS:
            rng = np.random.default_rng(302)
            centres, t, cl, n = time_resolved(area, value, binning, rng)
            TCURVE[(area, value, binning)] = pd.Series(t, index=np.round(centres, 3))
            for c in cl:
                R3EF.append(dict(area=area, value=value, binning=binning, neurons=n,
                                 sign="rem > forg" if c["sign"] == 1 else "rem < forg",
                                 start_s=centres[c["start"]], end_s=centres[c["end"]],
                                 cluster_sum=c["sum"], p=c["p"]))
            if not cl:
                R3EF.append(dict(area=area, value=value, binning=binning, neurons=n, sign="none"))
            print(area, value, binning, "neurons", n, "max |t| %.2f" % np.max(np.abs(t)),
                  "clusters", len(cl))
R3EF = pd.DataFrame(R3EF)
print("cluster tests took %.0f s" % (time.time() - t0))

Result: partially reproduced. Under every reading a cluster with remembered above forgotten has cluster p < 0.025, but it lies from about 0.875 to 1.05 s (p = 0.0001 to 0.0196), not from 0 to 650 ms. Clusters starting at maintenance onset do not reach significance (smallest p 0.061, 0 to 0.125 s, spikes per second, 200 ms windows). The time-resolved t shows why: in 0 to 650 ms it exceeds the cluster-forming threshold (about 2.0) at 3 of 27 points (normalized) and 6 of 27 (spikes per second) with 200 ms windows, with its largest values at onset (3.09 at 0 s, normalized; 3.47 at 0.025 s, spikes per second; windows that take in 100 and 75 ms of the last encoding picture), and at one of 13 points with 50 ms bins (2.13 and 2.32), too few contiguous points to form a significant cluster. The largest |t| over the whole delay lies at 0.925 to 1.025 s under every reading (4.05 and 4.41 with 200 ms windows, 3.43 and 3.60 with 50 ms bins). The criterion's partial grade is met, but the data do not support an early effect.

Claim fig3g-nonpreferred-no-effect¶

Maintenance activity of category neurons while non-preferred pictures are held does not predict later LTM accuracy or confidence.

The Figure 3a model on non-preferred rows: (a) every non-preferred picture of the code's table, (b) only pictures of trials that held no preferred picture.

In [37]:
trial_has_pref = {n: set(NPT[n].trial[NPT[n].pref == 1]) for n in ALL_CN}


def nonpref_b(d):
    d = fig3_select(d, pref=0)
    keep = [t not in trial_has_pref[n] for n, t in zip(d.neuron, d.trial)]
    return d[keep]

Claim ms-neuron-counts¶

Claim fig4b-ms-confidence-auc¶

Hippocampal memory-selective neurons separate old from new pictures better for high-confidence than for low-confidence decisions (higher ROC AUC), so they carry a memory-strength signal.

Spike counts 0.2 to 1.2 s after LTM picture onset. FS neurons: all true negatives against true positives rated 6 (high) and rated 4 or 5 (low); NS neurons: all true positives against true negatives rated 1 (high) and 2 or 3 (low); the AUC is oriented so that the preferred response above 0.5 is selectivity (sbcat.roc_auc). The all-sure session is left out. Neurons kept: (a) at least ten correct novel and ten correct familiar trials, (b) at least ten trials in each group compared; a neuron needs trials in both groups of each comparison; then O-M on the two AUC values.

In [40]:
MSH = K[(K.area == "hippocampus") & K.ms].copy()
rows = []
for _, u in MSH.iterrows():
    s = S[u.si]
    ltm = s["ltm"]
    c = sbcat.count(s["spikes"][u.ui], ltm.timestamps_PicOnset.values, 0.2, 1.2)
    conf, old = ltm.confidence.values, ltm.new_old.values == 1
    tp, tn = old & (conf >= 4), ~old & (conf <= 3)
    if u.ms_type == "FS":
        fixed, high, low = c[tn], c[tp & (conf == 6)], c[tp & ((conf == 4) | (conf == 5))]
        auc = lambda grp: sbcat.roc_auc(grp, fixed)
    else:
        fixed, high, low = c[tp], c[tn & (conf == 1)], c[tn & ((conf == 2) | (conf == 3))]
        auc = lambda grp: sbcat.roc_auc(grp, fixed)
    ok = len(high) > 0 and len(low) > 0 and np.r_[fixed, high, low].max() > 0
    rows.append(dict(neuron=f"{u.si}_{u.ui}", session=u.session, type=u.ms_type,
                     n_tp=int(tp.sum()), n_tn=int(tn.sum()), n_fixed=len(fixed), n_high=len(high),
                     n_low=len(low), auc_high=auc(high) if ok else np.nan,
                     auc_low=auc(low) if ok else np.nan, noconf=u.si in NOCONF_SI))
AUC = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print("hippocampal MS neurons:", len(AUC), " in the all-sure session:", int(AUC.noconf.sum()),
      " without trials in a compared group:", int(AUC.auc_high.isna().sum()))
rng = np.random.default_rng(401)
R4B = []
for lab, sel in [("(a) >= 10 TN and >= 10 TP", lambda a: (a.n_tp >= 10) & (a.n_tn >= 10)),
                 ("(b) >= 10 in each group compared",
                  lambda a: (a.n_fixed >= 10) & (a.n_high >= 10) & (a.n_low >= 10))]:
    a = AUC[sel(AUC) & ~AUC.noconf & AUC.auc_high.notna()]
    v = a[["auc_high", "auc_low"]].values
    out = np.any(np.abs(v - v.mean()) > 3 * v.std(ddof=1), axis=1)
    a = a[~out]
    t, p, df = sbcat.perm_ttest_paired(a.auc_high, a.auc_low, rng)
    R4B.append(dict(reading=lab, neurons=len(a), outliers=int(out.sum()), FS=int((a.type == "FS").sum()),
                    auc_high=a.auc_high.mean(), auc_low=a.auc_low.mean(), t=t, df=df, p=p))
print(pd.DataFrame(R4B).round(4).to_string(index=False))
print("paper: t(40) = 2.89, p = 0.0039, 41 neurons")
print("AUC range: %.3f to %.3f" % (np.nanmin(AUC[["auc_high", "auc_low"]].values),
                                   np.nanmax(AUC[["auc_high", "auc_low"]].values)))

Claim fig4d-category-no-memory-signal¶

During LTM retrieval, hippocampal category neurons code neither familiarity nor confidence for pictures of their preferred category.

The new pictures' categories are not in the dataset's metadata (see below). Their images are in the files, and viewing them gives the category of each: blocks of 40 IDs per category, in the order of the old pictures' leading digit.

LTM trials showing a picture of the neuron's preferred category; rate 0.2 to 1.2 s after picture onset. GLM on correct trials (all-sure session left out): FR ~ conf * old with the random intercepts of G. Readings: (D1) confidence coding (a) the code's or (b) certainty; (D2) rate (a) spikes per second or (b) normalized to the neuron's mean WM baseline (B1). The t-test: per neuron the mean rate of preferred old against preferred new pictures, (D3) (a) correct trials or (b) all trials, under both D2 readings, after O-M; paired permutation t-test.

The category of a new LTM picture is not in the dataset's metadata. New pictures have IDs 1001 to 1200 (old ones keep their WM IDs, whose leading digit is the category), and their images in the files (stimulus/templates/StimulusTemplates) are named only by ID. The three task variants show different sets of new pictures. In this revision all 600 new images (200 per variant, from the sessions below) were viewed one by one: in each variant IDs 1001 to 1040 show people (faces), 1041 to 1080 animals, 1081 to 1120 cars (variants 1 and 3) or tools (variant 2), 1121 to 1160 food and fruit, and 1161 to 1200 landscapes (with city views in variant 3), the same order as the leading digits 1 to 5 of the old pictures. No image was found outside its block. The cell below shows, per variant, eight old pictures of each leading digit and all 40 new pictures of the matching block, from the files, so the mapping can be checked; it also compares the images of two sessions of each variant, and then the new images of every session with those of the viewed session of its variant. The cell after it checks the mapping against the category neurons' responses: for each category neuron, the block with the highest mean response to new pictures is compared with its preferred category, against the same for old pictures and for a grouping by ID modulo 5.

def new_cat_block(ids):
    """Category of a new LTM picture: blocks of 40 IDs, from viewing the images (above)."""
    return (np.asarray(ids, int) - 1001) // 40 + 1


match = {"old pictures, category from the ID": 0, "new pictures, blocks of 40": 0,
         "new pictures, ID modulo 5": 0}
for _, u in CN.iterrows():
    s = S[u.si]
    l = s["ltm"]
    c = sbcat.count(NEURON_SPIKES[u.neuron], l.timestamps_PicOnset.values, 0.2, 1.2)
    new = l.new_old.values == 0
    ids = l.PicIDs.values.astype(int)
    for lab, sel, g in [("old pictures, category from the ID", ~new, ids // 100),
                        ("new pictures, blocks of 40", new, new_cat_block(ids)),
                        ("new pictures, ID modulo 5", new, (ids - 1001) % 5 + 1)]:
        m = [c[sel & (g == k)].mean() if np.any(sel & (g == k)) else -1 for k in range(1, 6)]
        match[lab] += int(np.argmax(m) + 1 == u.pref)
for k, v in match.items():
    print(f"{k}: the best group is the preferred category for {v} of {len(CN)} category neurons "
          f"({100*v/len(CN):.1f} %; chance 20 %)")

        d["FR"], d["confv"], d["old"] = d[d2], d[d1], d.old.astype(int)
        for orule in ("O-M", "O-C", "none"):
            bad = (sbcat.om_remove(d, ["old"], zero_col="c") if orule == "O-M" else
                   sbcat.oc_remove(d) if orule == "O-C" else set())
            m = sbcat.mixedlm(d[~d.neuron.isin(bad)], "confv * old")
            for term, r in m.iterrows():
                res.append(dict(D1=d1, D2=d2, outliers=orule, term=term, beta=r.beta, p=r.p,
                                neurons=m.attrs["neurons"], n=m.attrs["n"], converged=m.attrs["converged"]))

Every session's new images are identical to those of the viewed session of its variant (8809 images over 46 sessions, none differing), and every new picture shown in a session has its image in the file. The category neurons' responses agree: the best block is the preferred category for 58.0% of them, against 60.5% for old pictures and 16.4% for a grouping by ID modulo 5. With these categories no GLM effect reaches p < 0.05 under any reading (smallest p 0.079 with O-M, conf_cert and normalized rates; 0.063 with O-C), and no old against new t-test does (p 0.22 to 0.92, 96 or 98 neurons; paper t(94) = -0.28, p = 0.78).

Claims fig4e-fs-strong-maintenance and fig4f-ns-no-effect¶

Familiarity-selective hippocampal neurons respond more during LTM retrieval to familiar pictures that were held with strong, compared with weak, maintenance activity of a simultaneously recorded category neuron.

The response of novelty-selective hippocampal neurons to familiar pictures does not depend on whether the paired category neuron's maintenance activity was strong or weak.

Pairs of a hippocampal MS neuron and a hippocampal category neuron of the same session. Per category neuron, its maintenance rates in correct WM trials holding a preferred picture later shown in the LTM test, median-split within load 1 and within load 3 (a rate equal to the median is weak). The MS neuron's rate 0.2 to 1.2 s after onset of those pictures in the LTM test. Readings: (E1) the random intercept within patient is (a) the MS neuron or (b) the pair; (E2) (a) all LTM trials of those pictures or (b) those answered old; (E3) a neuron both MS and category (a) paired with itself or (b) not; (E4) rate (a) spikes per second or (b) normalized to the MS neuron's mean WM baseline.

In [46]:
MSN = K[(K.area == "hippocampus") & K.ms].copy()
MSN["neuron"] = [f"{a}_{b}" for a, b in zip(MSN.si, MSN.ui)]


def pair_rows(split="load"):
    """One row per (MS neuron, category neuron) pair and preferred picture. The category
    neuron's maintenance rates are median-split within each load (Methods) or, as a variant,
    over both loads pooled (split="pooled")."""
    prow = []
    for _, m in MSN.iterrows():
        sp = S[m.si]["spikes"][m.ui]
        trs = sbcat.add_counts(PT[m.si], sp)
        mbase = trs.groupby("trial").r_bsl.first().mean()
        for n in CN.neuron[(CN.area == "hippocampus") & (CN.si == m.si)]:
            pt = code_rows(NPT[n])
            pt = pt[(pt.acc == 1) & (pt.pref == 1)].copy()
            if len(pt) == 0:
                continue
            med = (pt.groupby("load").r_maint.transform("median") if split == "load"
                   else pt.r_maint.median())
            pt["strong"] = (pt.r_maint > med).astype(int)
            c = sbcat.count(sp, pt.t_ltm.values, 0.2, 1.2)
            prow.append(pd.DataFrame(dict(ms=m.neuron, cat=n, pair=f"{m.neuron}|{n}", patient=m.patient,
                                          type=m.ms_type, self=m.neuron == n, strong=pt.strong.values,
                                          load=pt.load.values, LTMacc=pt.LTMacc.values, c=c, Hz=c / 1.0,
                                          norm=sbcat.normalize(c / 1.0, mbase) if mbase > 0 else np.nan)))
    return pd.concat(prow, ignore_index=True)

def pair_tests(typ, rng, data=None):
    glm, tt = [], []
    for e2 in ("all", "answered old"):
        for e3 in ("with self", "without self"):
            for e4 in ("Hz", "norm"):
                d = P4 if data is None else data
                d = d[(d.type == typ) & d[e4].notna()]
                if e2 == "answered old":
                    d = d[d.LTMacc == 1]
                if e3 == "without self":
                    d = d[~d.self]
                d = d.assign(FR=d[e4])
                for e1 in ("MS neuron", "pair"):
                    dd = d.assign(neuron=d.ms if e1 == "MS neuron" else d.pair)
                    bad = sbcat.om_remove(dd.assign(neuron=d.pair), ["strong"], zero_col="c")
                    m = sbcat.mixedlm(dd[~d.pair.isin(bad)], "strong")
                    glm.append(dict(E1=e1, E2=e2, E3=e3, E4=e4, beta=m.loc["strong", "beta"],
                                    p=m.loc["strong", "p"], converged=m.attrs["converged"], pairs=d.pair[~d.pair.isin(bad)].nunique(),
                                    n=m.attrs["n"]))
                a = d[d.strong == 1].groupby("pair").agg(v=("FR", "mean"), c=("c", "sum"))
                b = d[d.strong == 0].groupby("pair").agg(v=("FR", "mean"), c=("c", "sum"))
                j = a.join(b, lsuffix="_s", rsuffix="_w", how="inner")
                j = j[(j.c_s > 0) & (j.c_w > 0)]
                v = j[["v_s", "v_w"]].values
                j = j[~np.any(np.abs(v - v.mean()) > 3 * v.std(ddof=1), axis=1)]
                t, p, df = sbcat.perm_ttest_paired(j.v_s, j.v_w, rng)
                tt.append(dict(E2=e2, E3=e3, E4=e4, pairs=len(j), strong=j.v_s.mean(), weak=j.v_w.mean(),
                               t=t, df=df, p=p))
    return pd.DataFrame(glm), pd.DataFrame(tt)


G4E, T4E = pair_tests("FS", np.random.default_rng(404))
G4F, T4F = pair_tests("NS", np.random.default_rng(405))

Result: not reproduced. In familiarity-selective pairs, MS responses after strong maintenance are not higher than after weak under any reading: the GLM betas are negative (-0.14 to -0.19 Hz, -6.5 to -9.4 normalized; p 0.059 to 0.45), and so are the paired t-tests (t from -1.00 to -1.60, p 0.11 to 0.33). There are 197 pairs (expected 198 +- 20) and 84 FS pairs (expected 76 +- 8). Per pair, strong minus weak has median -0.044 Hz, with 37 pairs positive and 47 negative (sign test p = 0.33); averaged per MS neuron, 9 of 20 are positive. With the median split over both loads pooled (a variant), strong is again below weak in all 24 readings, at p < 0.05 in four GLM readings and one t-test reading.

Result: blocked (methods underspecified). The readings the criterion names do not all give the same outcome, and the claims file blocks such a claim. No GLM reading reaches p < 0.05 (smallest 0.42), and seven of the eight t-test readings do not (p 0.14 to 0.98), but one does (pictures answered old, self-pairs dropped, spikes per second: t(81) = 2.04, p = 0.040), so the claim is neither reproduced (no p < 0.05 under every reading) nor not reproduced (p < 0.05 under every reading). Under all trials of the old pictures, self-pairs kept and spikes per second, the GLM gives beta 0.006 (p = 0.90) or 0.010 (p = 0.85) and the t-test t(106) = -1.03, p = 0.31, with 107 NS pairs (paper 122). The single p of 0.040 is one of 24 uncorrected tests.

Fits of the mixed models¶

statsmodels warned "invalid value in sqrt" during some fits (asked about in verification round 1). Each model is fitted with three optimizers and the fit with the highest likelihood is kept (sbcat.mixedlm). Below, for every table of results, the number of kept fits that did not report convergence and the number of rows with a missing SE or p.

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

How the analysis differs from the paper's. For the GLMs of Figures 2 and 3 the outlier rule is O-G, as the claims file has it after a reader's answer (questions/001187.yaml): the code's neuron means (NWB_computeGLM.m), with the Methods' "±3 SD from the mean"; the code's own rule (O-C, above 3 SD without centring) is shown as a variant, and gives the paper's Figure 3a betas within tolerance where O-G does not. The permutation t-tests keep the Methods rule (O-M). For Figure 2, which the code does not cover, the rows (one per trial or the code's), the baseline and, for Fig. 2c and 2f, the model (main effects or with the interaction) are open, and where they change the outcome the claim is blocked, as the claims file says. The session whose ratings are all sure is left out of confidence analyses, as the paper says; the code keeps it, shown as a variant. Mixed models are fitted by maximum likelihood in statsmodels, not MATLAB's fitglme. Permutation p-values follow statcond's formula. For Fig. 1d the permutation p is estimated with 2,000,000 permutations, as the criterion's bar (p < 0.0001) lies at the resolution of 10,000. For Fig. 4d the categories of the new pictures are taken from their images in the files, viewed one by one for this attempt.

What was found about the dataset. The 46 sessions, 950 units and the 351 and 532 units after the rate filter match the paper. Table S1 lists 23 more units in four sessions. All files give Cedars-Sinai as the institution, though the identifiers (TWH, JHU) and the paper place 20 sessions at Toronto Western and Johns Hopkins. Eight sessions have fewer than 400 LTM trials (161 to 399) and one has 139 WM trials. One LTM trial has confidence 7, outside the documented 1 to 6. The new LTM pictures (IDs 1001 to 1200) carry no category in the metadata; their images show blocks of 40 IDs per category in each task variant. Five units have spike times out of order in the files (sorted here before analysis). The confidence coding (1 to 3 new, 4 to 6 old) is not documented but agrees with the accuracy column in every trial.
